dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1808 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json: 125 items in 7 or more papers). Because several of the year's most printed documents sit in families that began in 1807, the same script was also run with year 1807 over the 1808 pages (items_from_1807.json: 54 items in 7 or more papers). Two AI reviewers read the items of each half of the year and proposed the stories; each item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 4,466 pages of 1808 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched with loose keywords, and the scan pages whose RevX text is filed under another page were read in the CA transcription. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As for 1776 and 1807: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs and items that need framing. Items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents, or several documents belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story. A sub-story may have fewer than 7 papers when its parent story reaches 7 (the rule the owner agreed for 1776 round two). A paper that printed an item again later counts each printing. Kentucky Gazette pages filed under 1808 are 1806 issues and were not used.
added_by_search: ADA 1808-03-25 p3: the President's message of 22 March, on a scan page whose own text survives only in the garbled CA transcription (the issue's RevX pages are filed one page off)
NI 1808-05-18 p3: the opening of the first Alicante letter (the item finder found its later part, printed by the paper on 20 May)

counted_item_by_item.Laws printed by authority: The item finder joins the embargo acts into chains (one item reaches 11 papers and 110 printings) because each supplementary act names the act it supplements and all share the enacting formula. Each act was counted by its own first section: the Embargo Act 5 papers in 1808, the act of 9 January 6, of 12 March 5, of 22 April 7, of 25 April 6. Bills printed before the acts were not counted, except a bill as passed by the Senate whose text is the act's (ADA 9 January; WR 5 May).
counted_item_by_item.The two Alicante letters: Two letters from Alicante, both dated 27 March 1808, were printed side by side (VA: 'Extract of another Letter'). The reviewers first took them for two parts of one letter in 8 papers; by their own wording each is in 7 papers, and each is its own group.
counted_item_by_item.The papers laid before Congress in March: About 45 items in the item lists are parts of one publication. They were grouped by the publication's own parts (the message; No. II, Canning and Monroe; No. III, Rose and Madison) and Champagny's letter, published separately on 2 April, each counted by its first document.
counted_item_by_item.Canning's speech of 24 June: Printed in two forms, a report ('The following observations were made by Mr. Canning…', 4 papers) and an 'Extract from Mr. Canning's speech' in his own words (3 papers); counted together as one speech, 7 papers.
counted_item_by_item.Jefferson's answer to the petitions: The same text was sent to several towns: 6 papers print the answer to Boston and the Portland Gazette the answer to Portland. Counted together, 7 papers.
counted_item_by_item.Commentary and debates: Pages that only quote an item (editorials, speeches, debate reports, later orders that recite an earlier one) were not counted: for example Campbell's report quoted in the Portland Gazette, Canning's letter of 23 September read out in Congress, the Orders in Council quoted in essays.

not_admitted.Laws and resolutions below 7 papers by t: The militia detachment act of 30 March (6 papers; the finder's 9 includes the list of acts), the act arming the militia and the act raising an additional military force (fewer than 7 each), the House resolution on when the embargo could be removed (January), and G. W. Campbell's resolution, which repeats the suspension act's words in debate reports.
not_admitted.The Supplemental Journal of the House (s: Procedural entries printed in parts; 9 papers only with the November reprint and both Alexandria titles.
not_admitted.Timothy Pickering's letter to Governor S: 6 papers; the New Hampshire Gazette prints only an answer that quotes it.
not_admitted.Canning's notice of the blockade of Cope: Not one item; the Foreign Office notice of 4 May is in 6 papers.
not_admitted.Article 12 of the French convention: A treaty article quoted inside different editorials, not an item.
not_admitted.News digests and mixed reports: The London paragraphs of 23 February on papers laid before the Commons, the outline of Parliament's proceedings in May, the Madrid paragraph on the Duke of Berg (August), the London paragraph on Joseph Bonaparte at Madrid (October), the news by the ship Camilla from Cadiz (October: two differently worded New York reports and several letters), and Lord Collingwood's letter and the 'Note 1' from Cadiz (two items of 6 papers each).
not_admitted.The resolutions of the committee on fore: Daily proceedings in which the resolutions recur (up to 27 printings), treated like a digest.
not_admitted.Other documents sent with the message of: Madison to Armstrong of 22 May and 8 February, the letters to Pinkney, Armstrong's letters of February and April: 5 to 7 papers each; three documents already stand for the set.
not_admitted.Candidates in 6 or 7 papers not chosen: The President's message of 4 February with Clark's papers (7); the message of 2 February sending the Orders in Council (4 by its text); the Navy Department's letter on seamen (7); Lord Grenville in the Lords on the Orders in Council, 5 May (7); the Liverpool 'Political Review' on Rose's return (7, a forecast); Jefferson's answer to the Democratic Ward of Philadelphia (about 5 in full); the table of how the states choose electors (5); Randolph's resolution for an inquiry into Wilkinson (4); Gallatin's letter on enforcing the embargo (6, December); the Treasury's certificate on the two millions (6); Joseph Bonaparte's proclamation (6); Champagny's report of 1 September (6).

for_user_decision.The Embargo Act's December 1807 printing: The act was first printed in late December 1807 (5 papers by the 1807 count). The site requires every printing of a reviewed year's group to fall in that year, so the 1808 group holds its 5 January printings only; across both years the act reaches 8 papers.
for_user_decision.Sub-stories below 7 papers: Four embargo laws (5, 6, 5, 6), the Order in Council of 11 November 1807 (6), the Cintra convention (6) and Canning's answer to Pinkney (6; the Enquirer says it printed it on 15 November, an issue the collection lacks), under parents that reach 7 or more.
for_user_decision.Two parents grouped by subject: 'Orders and decrees against neutral trade' and 'The embargo at home, spring 1808' group separate documents by subject.
for_user_decision.Two printed forms counted together: Canning's speech of 24 June (report and extract) and the President's answer to the petitions (to Boston and to Portland).
for_user_decision.The 'Melancholy Event' near Burlington,: Men of a revenue party killed by smugglers while enforcing the embargo; it names the dead and, later, the accused. Left out for framing.
for_user_decision.General Wilkinson's letters to Robert Go: A quarrel of honour published by Wilkinson. Left out.
for_user_decision.Governor Sevier's letter on the Creeks (: Needs framing first, like the Cherokee and Creek reports of 1776. Left out.
for_user_decision.Allegations in the Wilkinson story: Clark's statement and the Wilkinson-Randolph letters are allegations and personal attacks between public men in a public affair; the court of inquiry found no evidence. Admitted with the claims labelled.

data_issues.Kentucky Gazette issues filed two years: The 98 issues of sn84038147 filed under 1808 print 1806 in their mastheads (87 readable; the masthead weekday fits 1806); the 7 filed under 1806 are 1804 and the one filed 28 May 1807 is 1805. No 1808 story uses them. Evidence: outputs/story_discovery_1808/check_kentucky_gazette_dates.py and kentucky_gazette_dates.csv.
data_issues.Misfiled RevX pages: Three printings stand on scan pages whose RevX slot holds another page's text (derived/revx_page_map.parquet); their excerpts come from the CA transcription of the scan page: the Alexandria Daily Advertiser of 25 March (p. 3), the Norfolk Gazette of 20 June (p. 2) and the Alexandria Daily Gazette of 24 August (p. 3).

why.crops: The text-layer locator of work/scan_ledger.py crops from the excerpt's first words to its last. Where the last words also stand earlier (an act's title repeats its enacting clause) or the scan's text layer is garbled, the crop missed the passage. Such crops were cut again: from the start match and the excerpt's length (pdf_text_layer_span), from exact word sequences (pdf_text_layer_sequence) or from the window of the text layer that shares most of the excerpt's words (pdf_text_layer_window), and overlapping boxes in one column were merged; 18 boxes were placed by hand on gridded page images (manual_box). The boxes of all these crops are recorded in the ledger (scan_boxes), so work/scan_ledger.py can cut them again; the methods are in evidence/crop_manifest.json.
why.rechecks: Printings whose crop showed other text or only part of the item were checked again on their new crops (scan_verdicts/rechecks_1-4.json); those verdicts replace the batch verdicts.
why.S08-165: Graded fact-changing in rechecks_harmonise.json: 'intercept' for 'interrupt' is a different real word in the operative clause, by the rule applied to 'unmitigated' for 'unremitted'.
why.S08-120: The excerpt now starts at Rose's letter of 26 January, which a reviewer found at the top of the page's first column; the first excerpt had started at Madison's answer.
why.S08-199: The excerpt now ends at 'my crown,': the RevX transcription runs on into a footnote of the preceding document there.
